{{Quote|I've told you kids to slow down!|The woman, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="marvel">[[Star Wars (1977) 1|''Star Wars'' (1977) 1]]</ref>}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] '''female''' lived in the [[City/Legends|settlement]] of [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. She was aged by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], and she wore a metallic [[sun shawl]] to protect herself from the [[Tatoo I/Legends|twin]] [[Tatoo II/Legends|suns]] of the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system]].<ref name="EP4NOVEL" />

Late in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the [[Gender/Legends|woman]] was walking on a quiet, deserted street of Anchorhead when she was nearly run over by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], the nephew of a local [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]] named [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]]. The [[Farmer/Legends|farmboy]] was on his way to the [[Tosche Station/Legends|Tosche power station]] in his [[X-34 landspeeder/Legends|X-34 landspeeder]] to relate a [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|battle]] which he had spotted over their planet to his friends. The surprised woman quickly ran out of Skywalker's way and shouted after him, shaking her fist at the boy.<ref name="EP4NOVEL" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Won't you kids ever learn to slow down!|The woman's line in the novelization of ''A New Hope''|<ref name="EP4NOVEL" />}}
The woman appeared simply as "Woman" in the final script of the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> The character was played by a local Tunisian woman, and her scene was filmed during principal photography in front of a mosque in Djerba, Tunisia, on [[April 4]], [[1976]].<ref name="MOSW">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> Director [[George Lucas]] cut the scene before the release of the film, and no image of the scene was released until the [[1998]] [[Star Wars Insider 41|forty-first issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine published a still from it in the article "[[The Evolution of Star Wars: Exploring the Lost Cut]],"<ref name="ins41">{{InsiderCite|41|The Evolution of Star Wars: Exploring the Lost Cut|The Evolution of ''Star Wars'': Exploring the Lost Cut}}</ref> which raised the filmed version of the scene to G-[[canon]] status, the highest level of canonicity in the [[Star Wars|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.<ref name="cheeblog">{{Blog|holocron|33|What'd I say again? Select posts by me regarding continuity}}</ref>

[[File:Anchorhead_old_woman.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The old woman in ''Star Wars'' 1]]
The woman was also featured in three sources that adapted ''A New Hope''. Her first appearance, in which she uttered a slightly different line from the one spoken in the cut scene, was in the [[December]] 1976 [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of ''A New Hope'' by [[Alan Dean Foster]].<ref name="EP4NOVEL" /> She uttered the same line as in the script in two later sources: the [[Star Wars (1977) 1|first issue]] of [[Marvel Comics]]' [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] series,<ref name="marvel" /> published [[April 12]], 1977,<ref name="Marvel April">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/53791/star_wars_1977_1|text=Star Wars (1977) #1}}</ref> and the junior novel ''[[A New Hope: The Life of Luke Skywalker]]'', written by [[Ryder Windham]] and published in [[2009]].<ref name="life">''[[A New Hope: The Life of Luke Skywalker]]''</ref> As the latter two sources use the script-accurate line,<ref name="marvel" /><ref name="life" /> this article assumes that the novelization is in error.
